S76.01.note: Text input is not listed as its own item; the only visible sign is the absence of a chip and the Text only label, and routing to text-only handling was not confirmed in the UI.
steps: Click the model name button in the composer footer (its label ends in Change model).
In the Models dialog, click the About button on any model row.
Read the Capabilities line on the card.
Compare: every model accepts text, so text input has no chip of its own; a model with no other chip shows Text only.
S76.01.where: Models picker > About <model name> > Capabilities (text-only models show Text only)

S76.02.note: No separate text-output control or chip exists; text output is shown only by replies appearing in the chat.
steps: Click the model name button in the composer footer.
Click About on a model row.
Read the Capabilities line and check that a chat reply comes back as text.
S76.02.where: Models picker > About <model name> > Capabilities (text output is implied for every model)

S76.03.needs: a picture file to upload, a model without Vision and one with Vision
S76.03.note: The refusal alert text was found in ChatComposerNew.tsx; the exact send-blocking behaviour was not confirmed.
steps: Click the model name button in the composer footer and click About on a model without a Vision chip.
Close the picker, click More composer options and choose Add photos & files, then pick a JPG or PNG file.
Click Send or look at the composer alert.

Compare: the alert should read The selected model can't read the attached image. Switch to Auto, choose an image-capable model, or remove the image. Switch to a model with the Vision chip and the alert should not appear.
S76.03.where: Composer > More composer options > Add photos & files, then pick a picture; Models > About <model name> > Capabilities > Vision

S76.04.note: Per-request image count limits are enforced in apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/media-input.ts; no visible image-count message was found in the web composer.
steps: Click More composer options and choose Add photos & files.
Select several pictures in one go and click Send.
Compare: the request should go through or fail with a message about the image limit.
S76.04.where: Composer > Add photos & files with several pictures; the check runs when the request is sent

labels.text: The selected model can't read the attached document. Switch to Auto, choose a document-capable model, or remove the file.

S76.06.note: The alert is shown for models without document support; whether a PDF is sent natively to a document-capable model was not checked in the UI.
steps: Click the model name button and pick a model that cannot read documents.
Click More composer options and choose Add photos & files, then pick a PDF.
Click Send or look at the composer alert.

Compare: the alert should read The selected model can't read the attached document. Switch to Auto, choose a document-capable model, or remove the file. Switching to a document-capable model should remove the alert.
S76.06.where: Composer > More composer options > Add photos & files, then pick a PDF file

S76.07.note: Only the chip was found; no audio file attach control was located in the composer.
steps: Click the model name button in the composer footer.
Click About on a model row.
Look at the Capabilities chips on the card.
Compare: a model that accepts audio input shows an Audio in chip; other models do not.
S76.07.where: Models picker > About <model name> > Capabilities > Audio in

S76.08.needs: a microphone; a Free account may have dictation limits
S76.08.note: Privacy copy says recordings go to OpenAI for transcription; the choice of transcription model is not shown on screen.
steps: Open Settings and click Voice.
Turn on the Dictation switch and check Dictation language.
Close Settings, click the microphone button labelled Start voice input in the composer, and speak.
Compare: the spoken words should be added to the message text after transcription.
S76.08.where: Settings > Voice > Dictation; then the composer microphone button Start voice input

S76.09.needs: a microphone and a signed-in account
S76.09.note: The realtime model name is not shown on screen; the session route is in apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts.
steps: Click the button labelled Start voice mode in the composer.
Allow microphone access when asked.
Speak a short sentence and wait for a reply.
Compare: a live voice session should start and show the transcript turns of your speech.
S76.09.where: Composer > Start voice mode (icon button with a waveform)

S76.10.needs: a speaker and a browser with built-in voices
S76.10.note: Privacy copy says Read aloud uses the browser's built-in voices, not a registry-chosen model; this may differ from Expected.
steps: Get a text reply from the assistant.
Click the More message actions button under the reply.
Click Read message aloud.
Compare: the reply should be read aloud, and the menu item should change to Stop reading message while speaking.
S76.10.where: Assistant reply > More message actions > Read message aloud

S76.11.needs: a microphone, speakers and a signed-in account
S76.11.note: The speech-to-speech model is not named on screen; confirm the spoken reply in the live session.
steps: Click Start voice mode in the composer.
Allow the microphone and ask a question out loud.
Listen for the spoken answer.
Compare: the reply should be spoken back during the live session, not only written in the chat.
S76.11.where: Composer > Start voice mode, then speak and listen for the spoken reply

S76.14.needs: none; a plan may limit image creation
S76.14.note: Image output is also listed as an Image out chip on each model card in the Models picker.
steps: Click More composer options in the composer.
Click Create image.
Type a short picture prompt and send it.
Compare: an image should be generated; if the chosen model cannot make images, the image mode should not start.
S76.14.where: Composer > More composer options > Create image

S76.15.note: The warning Image mode takes images only was found in ChatComposerNew.tsx; which image models accept edits is not shown in the picker.
steps: Click More composer options and choose Create image.
Click More composer options again and choose Add photos & files, then pick a picture.
Type an edit instruction and send.
Compare: the edited picture should come back; the composer should warn if the file is not a picture.
S76.15.where: Composer > More composer options > Create image, then Add photos & files to attach a picture

S76.17.needs: none; a plan may limit video creation
S76.17.note: No duration or size control was located in the composer code reviewed; check the screen after choosing Create video.
steps: Click More composer options and choose Create video.
Type a short video prompt and check the duration or size controls.
Send the request.
Compare: the video should match the duration and size offered for the chosen model.
S76.17.where: Composer > More composer options > Create video

S76.19.note: No audio on/off control was found; the effect is only visible in the finished video file.
steps: Create a short video with Create video.
Download or open the finished video.
Compare: the video should have a sound track only if the model that made it supports audio.
S76.19.where: Generated video file after Composer > More composer options > Create video

S76.21.note: The refusal or rerouting of tool turns to models without Tools was not confirmed in the UI.
steps: Click the model name button in the composer footer.
Click About on a model row.
Look for the Tools chip in Capabilities.
Compare: a model with function calling shows Tools; a model without it does not.
S76.21.where: Models picker > About <model name> > Capabilities > Tools

S76.22.needs: a Connector or tool that the model can use
S76.22.note: No visible setting for parallel tool calls was found.
steps: Ask a question that needs two tools at once, such as a search plus a file lookup.
Watch the tool steps shown under the reply.
Compare: the tool steps should run together when the model supports parallel tool calls.
S76.22.where: Chat reply that uses several tools in one step (effect seen in the reply)

S76.23.needs: a Connector or tool that the model can use
S76.23.note: The only visible label is the Tools chip on the model card, which is function calling rather than agentic rounds.
steps: Ask a question that needs a search, then a follow-up tool use, such as a file lookup.
Watch the reply for several tool rounds before the final answer.
Compare: the model should use more than one tool round when needed.
S76.23.where: Chat reply that calls tools over several rounds (effect seen in the reply)

S76.26.needs: a Free or paid account; a model with reasoning effort levels
S76.26.note: The Off note text is Off is not supported by this model in ComposerFooter.tsx.
steps: Open the model picker from the composer footer and pick a model that supports reasoning effort.
Click the Reasoning effort control in the composer footer and look at the levels offered.
Open Settings > General and find Reasoning effort.
Compare: only the levels that the chosen model supports should appear; Off should show a note if the model cannot turn reasoning off.
S76.26.where: Composer footer > Reasoning effort control; Settings > General > Reasoning effort

S76.28.note: Trimming or refusing over-long requests was not confirmed in the UI.
steps: Click the model name button in the composer footer.
Click About on a model row.
Read the Context ceiling value in the grid of facts.
Compare: the value should match the model's context window; a very long chat should be trimmed or refused.
S76.28.where: Models picker > About <model name> > Context ceiling

S76.29.note: The effect on long replies was not confirmed in the UI.
steps: Click the model name button in the composer footer.
Click About on a model row.
Read the Output ceiling value.
Compare: the value should match the model's output limit, and a very long reply should stop at that size.
S76.29.where: Models picker > About <model name> > Output ceiling

S76.31.note: No streaming on/off control was found; the transport choice is inside the request path.
steps: Send a long question to a model.
Watch the reply text while it is still arriving.
Compare: the text should appear piece by piece rather than all at once.
S76.31.where: Chat reply as it is written (effect seen while the answer arrives)

S76.32.needs: a chat with at least one reply
S76.32.note: The cache class per route is not shown; only the switch warning is visible.
steps: Send a message and wait for a reply in a chat.
Click the model name button in the composer footer and pick a different model.
Look at the line just above the composer footer.
Compare: the line Switching models here starts a new prompt cache should appear once there are earlier turns.
S76.32.where: Composer, after at least one reply in the chat: switch model with the model name button

S76.34.note: Searched for region, residency and countries; the only match was Allowed countries in apps/web/features/workspace-console/components/WorkspaceFeatureControls.tsx, which is not shown as model or provider residency in the picker.

S76.35.note: The admin page path from the sidebar was not confirmed; the routing effect is inner behaviour and is not visible on screen.

Find the Zero data retention only switch.
Turn it on and save.
Compare: routes that keep data should be excluded for chats in this workspace; this routing effect is not shown on the page itself.

S76.37.needs: none; the Leaving text appears only in the warning window before retirement
S76.37.note: Retired models are excluded from the list in routing code, but the picker label for them was not located.
steps: Click the model name button in the composer footer to open the Models dialog.
Look at the status text on each model row.
Compare: a model with a scheduled retirement shows Leaving <date>; a model that is down shows Unavailable right now, and it cannot be picked.
S76.37.where: Models picker: model row status text (Leaving <date> or Unavailable right now)

labels.text: Switching models here starts a new prompt cache

S76.38.needs: a Free account or a paid account, and a chat with at least one reply
S76.38.note: Expected asks for per-route cache class, retention, price and routing rank. The Code line cites ComposerFooter.tsx:1571 (the catalogue open branch, no route text) and auto.ts:1099 and 1169 (route rejection reasons and cache-affinity ranking, internal only). Searched for route, cacheClass and cache text in apps/web, apps/desktop, packages/ui and packages/ai; the route data lives in the generated model registry (packages/ai/model-registry), not in any visible control. The plan note says "not written yet".
steps: Sign in and open a chat that already has at least one reply.
Open the model picker in the composer footer and look at its bottom area.

Check that the line "Switching models here starts a new prompt cache" is shown, and that it is absent on a new empty chat. This line is about cache reset on model switch, not per-route differences; the route ranking itself has no visible effect in the UI.
S76.38.where: No screen shows route-specific capabilities, cache class, retention or price. The only related visible text is a line in the chat model picker: "Switching models here starts a new prompt cache", shown after a chat has at least one assistant reply.
